notes: Battle Royale preset taken whole. `collectible-loot` is kept but sits awkwardly with the prompt, which says better guns are bought with Isaac balloons rather than found on the ground.

`building-interior` comes from the preset, not from the prompt, and it is what puts P3 on this build. Nothing the user wrote requires going indoors, so this is the cheapest thing to drop if P3 is unavailable.
`social-hub` and `teleporter-link` taken from `options.md` (worded by 6 genres each); Shooter's own table has no lobby row and no lobby-to-arena transition row.
`teleporter-link` is one of the *varies* rows. Routed P0 — one map with the lobby in it — because the prompt never says the lobby is a separate place. P4 if it is.
`options.md` does not carry the `Type (Flavor Name)` form, so `layout_placement.type` for `teleporter-link` could not be filled and is null.
The run's end is 'be last standing', which has no place attached to it. No `winner-zone` emitted; `boundary-shrinking` is what terminates the round spatially.
Scale set from the detail rule rather than the extent: the finest thing that matters is a breachable building, which is the Block band, even though battle royale is listed as typical of Region.

skill_gap.name: emit fields the reference files do not carry
skill_gap.why: The emit format wants `type` and `name` for the shape and a Shared Vocabulary `type` for every layout placement, but a genre file lists shapes as bare IDs and `options.md` has no name column at all. Getting `open-battlefield`'s `Zone (Open Battlefield)` needed `shapes.md`, which step 2 says not to load by default, and `teleporter-link`'s type could not be filled from any file in scope.

notes_for_us: A genre file's Typical shapes line gives bare IDs, but emit needs `type` and `name` — so every shape outside the genre's 'Its own wording' table forces the shapes.md load step 2 tells you to avoid.
options.md has no `Type (Flavor Name)` column, so any option taken from the catalogue cannot fill layout_placement.type.
'Take the whole preset' collides with step 4's 'prefer P0/P6': Battle Royale's building-interior put P3 on a prompt that never mentions going indoors.

Intake says to ask about scale only when an extent is named without contents; it gives no rule for a prompt silent on both, and the band table's 'typical of battle royale = Region' fights its own 'detail wins' rule.
Step 4 says to infer the place the run ends from the genre, but battle royale's ending has no place — last standing happens wherever the boundary closes. No rule covers that.
